claims.text: The route actually driven was 18.0 km against a recommended route of 16.7 km, a deviation of 1.30 km, which is over the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets; the deviation is therefore outside tolerance and the trip sits past the line at which POL-RD-24's refund matrix bites.

The reroute was not traffic-justified. The LTA advisory for the Ayer Rajah Expressway towards Tuas over the trip window reports type NONE and states that no incident, roadwork or closure was recorded for the queried segment, and NONE is not one of the closure, congestion or incident types POL-RD-23 names; the advisory's own derived field puts justifies_reroute at false. A driver's bare assertion of conditions is expressly not enough under POL-RD-23.

The driver did not tell the rider about the deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires him to do before or at the point of deviation. The chat log holds exactly two messages — the driver's 'Uncle please stop kicking my seat' at 00:06:43 and the rider's reply at 00:07:53 — both sent before the deviation was detected at 00:10:43, and neither says anything about a reroute, a closure, a blocked road or a change of route. The trip record's in_app_calls array is empty, so there is no recorded verbal notice either, and POL-RD-21 does not allow an unrecorded verbal notice to be established.

On those facts the trip falls into row (d) of the POL-RD-24 matrix — not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km — which is a refund of the excess distance fare in full. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate without surge: 1.30 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 0.94 SGD, the figure the fare breakdown itself records.

That 0.94 SGD is already with the rider: the ledger shows payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED and refund_issued_sgd 0.94, and the trip record shows a fare_adjusted event at 2026-10-03T03:31:59 refunding 0.94 SGD to the rider and recovering it from the driver. The driver now asks for that money back, and the present payment state is the one that matches the matrix. Under POL-GEN-03 a claim the record does not support leaves the present state standing as NO_ACTION, and NO_ACTION here is the ruling that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge and the driver with nothing to recover.

The driver's own account does not rescue his claim. POL-RD-24 has no safety limb — its rows turn on traffic justification and on notification, not on why the driver chose another road — and POL-RD-23 requires traffic data for the recommended segment rather than a driver's statement. Even taken at its highest, the driver's narrative that he left the AYE at Clementi Road for a better lit road fits no row of the matrix other than row (d).

The contested amount is 0.94 SGD. That is far below the 10.00 SGD band in POL-GEN-22, so an AI ruling on the merits is final at any confidence, and the deviation of 1.30 km is inside POL-RD-25's 2 km limb (which is not applied in any event — ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false). Nothing in the decision rules puts this dispute beyond an AI ruling on the merits.

Honest disclosure: the dispute carries a safety flag and the chat log contains the rider's express words 'Shut up and drive or I give you one punch', so POL-GEN-21 requires this case to go to human review whatever the category chosen — the rider's denial of any threat in his statement is not borne out by the log. That referral is not a loss for the rider on the money: an escalation issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount, so it cannot hand the 0.94 SGD back to the driver. The refund the matrix requires stays where the ledger has already put it.

claims.text: This dispute is safety-flagged and the record itself carries a threat of assault, so it is not the AI's to decide. The rider's own in-app message MSG-06011-002, sent 00:07:53, delivered 00:07:54 and read 00:08:26, reads 'Shut up and drive or I give you one punch'; the chat log is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, not truncated, and the message is unredacted with a read receipt. POL-GEN-21 requires a dispute flagged as safety-related, or whose record carries verbal harassment or a threat of assault or a driver feeling unsafe, to be escalated to human review whatever category the filer chose, and it forbids the AI from issuing a ruling, determining fault or recommending a resolution on it. On that clause the 0.94 SGD recovered from the driver is held for the reviewer rather than left standing with the rider under a NO_ACTION.

The rider's counterparty statement - 'The driver took a longer route on purpose. I never threatened anybody.' - is contradicted by his own words in the platform chat log, so the account on which the route complaint rests does not survive the record. The same log shows the driver raising the passenger's conduct in the cabin in the in-app channel at 00:06:43 ('Uncle please stop kicking my seat', delivered 00:06:45, read 00:06:55), a minute and ten seconds before the threat, and four minutes before the deviation. That is the conduct POL-GEN-21 names, and it is the driver's ground for leaving the expressway - not an unexplained detour.

The driver's device trace fixes the deviation in time and place exactly as the driver describes it, and shows driving, not meter-running. The vehicle left the recommended route at the AYE / Clementi Road exit at 00:10:43, three minutes after the rider's threat; it ran Clementi Road and Upper Bukit Timah Road continuously - every intermediate fix reports a speed between 33 and 56 kph, with no stationary fix between the first and the last of the 49 fixes - and rejoined at Bukit Batok East Avenue 6 / Upper Bukit Timah Road at 00:19:48. POL-RD-22 makes the trace the record of which route was taken and when. It shows a driver taking a lit, populated road to end a threatening trip, which is the account he filed, not a driver leaving the route to inflate the fare.

On the platform's own recorded distances the deviation is 18.0 km minus 16.7 km, i.e. 1.30 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22, and the excess distance fare at 1.30 km x 0.72 SGD/km is 0.94 SGD - the exact sum already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver. Whatever a reviewer does with the refund matrix, these figures cap the driver's exposure on this trip at the 0.94 SGD already taken: there is no arithmetic basis on this record for any further recovery from the driver, and the question for review is whether that clawback should stand.

The only traffic data in the case runs the other way, and the driver does not claim otherwise: the LTA advisory for the AYE segment (Clementi Road to PIE, towards Tuas) that overlaps the trip window records type NONE - no incident, roadwork or closure, speed bands 6-8 - so the reroute is not traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. That does not decide this case against the driver; it removes the traffic row. The refund matrix in POL-RD-24 is drafted on the traffic axis, and the deviation here is safety-driven, so the case fits no row of that matrix, and POL-RD-24 expressly sends a case that fits no row to escalation under POL-GEN-26. The right destination for a deviation taken because the passenger had just threatened the driver is a human reviewer, not a matrix row that never contemplated it.

Whether the driver told the rider he was leaving the AYE cannot be established from this record, and POL-GEN-26 says what to do with a fact the record cannot establish. POL-RD-21 permits notice of a deviation verbally at the point of deviation with the trip call recording as evidence, and it provides in terms that a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established. The trip record's in_app_calls array is empty and the chat log carries only the two messages above, neither of which is a notice of deviation - but a verbal notice at the wheel leaves no artifact by design. That open question is for the human reviewer; the AI must not resolve it against the driver by inferring silence from the absence of a recording.

The present state is provisional and the platform recorded it as such: the fare_adjusted event at 03:31:59 reads 'Interim adjustment after a rider route complaint: SGD 0.94 refunded to rider and recovered from driver earnings pending review'. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative and would simply preserve that clawback, leaving the driver's 0.94 with the rider without any finding that the driver did anything wrong; ESCALATE instead holds the amount for the human reviewer. On a record the platform itself marked 'pending review', and on which the driver filed at 05:06:59 - an hour and a half later - the 0.94 SGD should go to that review and not be finalised against the driver.
